steps.say: Welcome to RehearseLines. If you've ever tried to practice a scene on your own, you know how easy it is to lose the rhythm without someone reading the other parts.
steps.label: Introduction to RehearseLines

steps.say: RehearseLines gives you a scene partner in your browser. You can organize a show, bring in a script, and hear the other characters read their lines while you practice yours.
steps.label: Your scene partner

steps.say: I'll start on the dashboard and create a production. This one is a play called The Clockwork Curtain. A production keeps this show's scenes, cast, and rehearsal settings together.
steps.label: Create a production

steps.say: Now I'll open Rehearse, go to Scenes, and choose Import Scenes. I'll paste a short original scene for this demo. You can also start with a file using Upload File.
steps.label: Import a script

steps.say: I'll parse the text and check the character names before creating the scene. This gives me a chance to correct anything the app couldn't identify on its own.
steps.label: Review the cast

steps.say: Over in Cast, there are the two characters, Mara and Eli. I can manage each character here. I'll open Eli's voice settings and give him a voice.
steps.label: Assign a voice

steps.say: Now I'll open Run Lines, pick the scene, and choose Mara as my character. I'll leave it on Pause and wait, so I can take my turn at my own pace.
steps.label: Set up a rehearsal

steps.say: I'll start the scene. The app waits on Mara's line. When I'm ready, I'll move on and let it read Eli's reply.
steps.label: Run the scene

steps.say: One thing to know before you start your own show. Productions and imported scripts are saved locally in the browser you use. That keeps scripts private by default and helps avoid distributing copyrighted material.
steps.label: Stored in this browser

steps.say: Here's the same site in a fresh browser. The Clockwork Curtain isn't on this list. Switching browsers or devices doesn't bring your productions over automatically.
